newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: EML's rescuers see creditors fully paid.
newsitem.headline: EML's rescuers see creditors fully paid.

text.p: Price Waterhouse, judicial managers for ailing video cassette maker Electro Magnetics (1992) Ltd (EML), said on Monday creditors would get 100 percent of debts due if a provisional rescue plan is approved.
The managers told a news conference the rescue plan would see creditors paid in full, adding that "shareholders would walk away with something too".

The proposed Singapore $88 million rescue plan would provide shareholders with a payment of Singapore 16.8 cents for each of the roughly 340 million EML shares outstanding and give creditors the estimated S$30 million they are due. The S$30 million was a capped figure said the managers.
An additional cash injection of S$1.5 million would also be made, said the managers.
The provisional rescue deal provide initial payments of 20 percent in cash, 20 percent in shares in the new rescue vehicle with the 60 percent balance repaid over five years.
The managers said the rescue vehicle would guarantee profits at S$15 million after tax for the next three years.

The provisional deal has been put together with businessman Joseph Gondobintoro, a Singapore permanent resident whose investment vehicle Panwell Pte Ltd would create a new company -- "Newco" -- to take control of ailing EML.
Shares in EML have been suspended since July 1995 and judicial managers were appointed in October 1996 after a bailout plan fell through.
Under the planned rescue deal Newco would guarantee to have assets of not less than S$165 million, comprised of holdings in companies in which Gondobintoro has existing interests.

These ventures include an electronics, audio and video tape manufacturer and distributor and a paper and box manufacturer, both based in Indonesia, an automobile distributor and a company which runs rubber plantations in Africa.
Newco would also control the site of the GMG Building at 108 Robinson Road in Singapore's financial district.
The existing business of EML was unlikely to be continued by Newco, which would be likely to enter the business sectors of its new primary asset backers, the managers said
The managers said Newco would apply for a listing on SESDAQ.
It is expected that the deal, which must be signed and become official by Gondobintoro by January 31 and then be approved by various parties, would take up to four months to complete.
